evals.prompt: I have 36 photos of a watch shot on a turntable, currently named IMG_4501.jpg through IMG_4536.jpg. Get them working as a 360 spin on our Sirv account and embed it on the product page.
evals.expected_output: Renames files to a clean ascending sequence in one folder per product, uploads to Sirv so the .spin auto-generates, embeds with Sirv JS + class=Sirv markup, adds preconnect and layout space, and verifies rotation order, zoom, and mobile swipe behavior.
expectations: Places frames in one folder with a clean single ascending number sequence
Relies on Sirv auto-generation of the .spin file
Embeds with Sirv JS and class=Sirv markup, with preconnect for above-fold use
Warns about extra digit groups in filenames being read as rows
Verifies rotation order, zoom, and mobile scroll vs swipe

evals.prompt: Our spin feels sluggish and heavy on mobile - it has 120 frames at 5000px each. Improve it.
evals.expected_output: Reduces to ~36 frames, keeps masters 2500-4000px and lets Sirv handle delivery compression, checks autospin/zoom settings, keeps spinOnAnyDrag off on mobile, and verifies weight and interaction after changes.
expectations: Reduces frame count toward the 24-36 sweet spot
Does not destroy masters; relies on Sirv delivery resizing/compression
Keeps mobile vertical scrolling working (spinOnAnyDrag off)
Verifies load weight and interaction after the change

evals.prompt: We only have a video of the product rotating - can we get a 360 spin from it programmatically for 200 SKUs?
evals.expected_output: Uses the video2spin API with sensible frame count (36) and JPEG output, respects plan hourly conversion limits and the 512MB/300MB video size guidance, organizes one folder per SKU, and spot-checks converted spins.
expectations: Uses POST /v2/files/video2spin via the sirv-api skill rather than manual conversion
Chooses a sensible frame count and JPEG output for weight
Accounts for hourly conversion limits per plan and file size limits
Verifies converted spins by spot-checking frames and rotation
